official.status_note: IUJ's September 2027 admission schedule is published and applications are made through the IUJ Online Application System; the first application round closes 10 December 2026 for Master's programmes and 16 November 2026 for the PhD programme.
official.tuition_coverage_note: Nakayama Premium: 100% tuition, partial admissions fee, and a JPY 100,000 monthly stipend, for Master's students and PhD students.
benefits: Available to Master's students and PhD students

selection_criteria: Scholarships are awarded competitively at the time of admission, based on the goals of IUJ's partner organizations, companies and foundations
application_method: Read the Admissions Guidelines and Scholarship Guidelines in Brochures & Admissions Materials

official.application_route: No separate scholarship form: register as 'Non-Sponsored' in the IUJ Online Application System, complete the Scholarship Section in Phase 2, and the award is decided with the admission result
official.citizenship_residency: Published for non-Japanese (international) applicants; most IUJ scholarships require recipients to hold a Japan Student Visa
official.duration: Master's programmes run one or two academic years depending on the programme (one-year programmes such as the GSIM MBA/Digital Transformation, or two-year programmes such as the GSIR International Development and Public Management programmes); the PhD programme has its own application rounds
official.description: The Nakayama Premium is an IUJ scholarship for non-Japanese applicants listed under IUJ's Scholarship Guidelines, covering 100% of tuition, a partial admissions fee and a JPY 100,000 monthly stipend. It is awarded competitively at the time of admission to Master's and PhD students who apply as non-sponsored applicants.
official.program_type: University-funded admission scholarship (International University of Japan)
official.english_requirement: TOEFL, IELTS or TOEIC, unless exempted under IUJ's English Test Exemption Policy: four years of English-medium secondary education in Australia, Canada, Ireland, New Zealand, the UK or the USA (any nationality), or an undergraduate or graduate degree completed at an institution where the language of instruction is English, with evidence of the medium of instruction (a transcript alone is insufficient unless it clearly states the institution's language)

applicant_utility.summary: There is no separate Nakayama Premium application: you register as 'Non-Sponsored' in the IUJ Online Application System and complete the Scholarship Section in Phase 2, then the award is decided alongside admission. The stipend of JPY 100,000 per month sits on top of full tuition and a partial admissions fee, but IUJ's own budget table puts a single student's first academic year at roughly JPY 4.5-5.3 million, so expect to self-fund a substantial gap. Round choice matters: the PhD first round closes 16 November 2026, two months before the Master's first round on 10 December 2026.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Non-sponsored applicants to an IUJ Master's or PhD place whose tuition is fully covered by this award and who can evidence English proficiency or qualify for the exemption.
application_readiness_checklist: Target the earliest round you can complete cleanly - PhD 16 November 2026, Master's 10 December 2026 - because scholarships are decided at the time of admission
Register in the IUJ Online Application System with sponsorship status 'Non-Sponsored'; sponsored applicants are not considered for this scholarship
Complete the Scholarship Section in Phase 2 - skipping it removes you from scholarship consideration
Prepare TOEFL/IELTS/TOEIC scores, or assemble English-medium education evidence (a transcript alone is not enough unless it clearly states the medium of instruction)
Budget for the gap between the JPY 100,000 monthly stipend and IUJ's published first-year cost estimate before accepting a place
common_rejection_risks: Registering as sponsored instead of 'Non-Sponsored', which takes you out of contention for IUJ's non-Japanese applicant scholarships
Forgetting the Scholarship Section in Phase 2 and receiving an admission offer without any scholarship
Applying for a later round when earlier-round scholarship decisions are already committed
Assuming an English-medium degree exempts you automatically - the evidence of medium of instruction must be submitted
Counting on a visa-incompatible funding plan: most IUJ scholarships require recipients to hold a Japan Student Visa
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: The remaining share of the admissions fee, flights to Japan, and living costs beyond the JPY 100,000 monthly stipend - IUJ's published first-year budget for a single student runs about JPY 4,504,000-5,348,000 depending on programme.
document_audit: English-medium instruction evidence must come from the degree-granting institution; an ordinary transcript is rejected unless it states the language of instruction explicitly
The online application is phased: Phase 1 admission materials, then the Scholarship Section in Phase 2 - document everything for both before the round closes
GSIM applicants note that those submitting GMAT/GRE scores are not interviewed, so test dates feed directly into round planning
alerts: PhD and Master's deadlines differ (16 November 2026 vs 10 December 2026 for the first round) - confirm which programme you are applying to
Scholarships are tied to admission rounds; a stronger scholarship earlier beats waiting for a later round
Most IUJ scholarships, including this one, require a Japan Student Visa, so plan the student visa route before enrolment
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Single IUJ Online Application System account, 'Non-Sponsored' registration, Phase 1 materials plus the Phase 2 Scholarship Section, then the admission and scholarship decision per round.
